 if condition

Add an underscore in amdgpu_trace.h line 24 "_AMDGPU_TRACE_H".

Fixes: d38ceaf99ed0 ("drm/amdgpu: add core driver (v4)")
Reviewed-by: Guchun Chen <guchun.chen@amd.com>
Reviewed-by: Paul Menzel <pmenzel@molgen.mpg.de>
Signed-off-by: Chenyang Li <lichenyang@loongson.cn>
Signed-off-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.deucher@amd.com>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_trace.h b/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_trace.h
index 6752d8b13118..ce8dc995c10c 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_trace.h
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_trace.h
@@ -21,7 +21,7 @@
  *
  */
 
-#if !defined(_AMDGPU_TRACE_H) || defined(TRACE_HEADER_MULTI_READ)
+#if !defined(_AMDGPU_TRACE_H_) || defined(TRACE_HEADER_MULTI_READ)
 #define _AMDGPU_TRACE_H_
 
 #include <linux/stringify.h>
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_trace.h`**
   - The preprocessor condition on line 24 was modified. The macro name `_AMDGPU_TRACE_H` was changed to `_AMDGPU_TRACE_H_`. This change ensures that the macro is correctly defined with an underscore at the end.

### Relationships
- The modification in `amdgpu_trace.h` addresses a bug related to the preprocessor condition that checks for the definition of the macro. The fix is linked to a previous commit identified by the hash `d38ceaf99ed0`, which introduced the core driver. The change was reviewed and approved by multiple individuals, indicating that it is a necessary correction to ensure proper functionality of the driver.

The macro `_AMDGPU_TRACE_H` is incorrectly defined without a trailing underscore, which causes the preprocessor condition to fail in recognizing the macro's definition. This can lead to multiple inclusions of the header file, resulting in redefinition errors or unexpected behavior in the code that relies on this macro for conditional compilation.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#if !defined(_AMDGPU_TRACE_H_) || defined(TRACE_HEADER_MULTI_READ)
#define _AMDGPU_TRACE_H_
```
Reason:

This prevents multiple inclusions of the header file, thereby avoiding potential redefinition errors and ensuring the intended behavior of the code that depends on this macro.
